title: New York Fashion Week: An intimate, unfiltered look at seriously fun clothes | CNN
text:
Brands leaned into their signature codes — whether it be designer of the momentHenry Zankovand his simultaneous refresh of Diane von Furstenburg’s classic wrap dress and his own namesake label, Zankov, or Eckhaus Latta throwing a loft party complete with mesh outfits meant for misbehaving and freaky PVC footwear gliding across confetti-sprinkled hardwood floors. Thom Browne meanwhile invited guests to theoretically touch grass with a gargantuan gardenscape presentation complete with impeccably tailored insect-inspired outfits. It was a welcome reminder that all of this is meant to be simultaneously fabulous andfun.

There were still moments of good old fashioned runway enchantment.Carolina Herrera marked 45 years in businesswith models gracing a runway in the spectacular David H. Koch theater filled to the brim with planted tulips. Daniella Kallymeyer served up tailored bar jackets, sultry knits, and sumptuous satin blouses — a refreshing interpretation of aspirational minimalism that was far more interesting than any form of “quiet luxury.” Sandy Liang continued to stress that unapologetic femininity is far from a fault (and that she truly understands a downtown girl’s penchant for polka dot bombers and tutu midi skirts). And industry darling Rachel Scott of Diotima and Proenza Schouler kept on playing with sartorial sex appeal, using eye-catching texture, bold print work and fabulously furry detailing with aplomb.

Below are some of the looks –– and unfiltered moments –– we saw.
